The 2026 season was Mumbai Indians' nineteenth appearance in the Indian Premier League (IPL). They were one of the ten cricket teams that competed in the 2026 IPL. The team was captained by Hardik Pandya and coached by Mahela Jayawardene.

Mumbai Indians were the second team to be eliminated from the 2026 IPL and finished the season in ninth place with four wins from 14 matches. Ryan Rickelton scored the most runs (448) while Allah Ghazanfar took the most wickets (15) for Mumbai in the 2026 season.

Pre-season

[edit | edit source]
Further information: List of 2026 Indian Premier League personnel changes

The 2026 Indian Premier League was the 19th edition of the Indian Premier League (IPL), a professional Twenty20 (T20) cricket league held in India, organised by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).[5] Mumbai Indians are the joint-most successful franchise with 5 title wins.[6] The team finished in fourth place in the previous season.[7] The tournament featured ten teams competing in 74 matches from 28 March to 31 May 2026.[8][9][10] Mumbai played all their home matches at Wankhede Stadium.[11]

Player retention

[edit | edit source]

Franchises were allowed to retain any number of players from their squad.[12] Franchises were required to submit their retention lists before 15 November 2025.[13] Mumbai retained twenty players, including captain Hardik Pandya and former captain Rohit Sharma.[14][15][16] Mumbai traded in Shardul Thakur from Lucknow Super Giants, Sherfane Rutherford from Gujarat Titans and Mayank Markande from Kolkata Knight Riders.[17][18][19] Mumbai also traded Arjun Tendulkar to Lucknow.[20]

Auction

[edit | edit source]

The season's auction took place on 16 December 2025 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.[23] The auction purse for each franchise was set at ₹125 crore (US$13 million),[14] with franchises being deducted an amount from the purse for every retained player.[12][24] Mumbai had a purse remaining of ₹2.75 crore (US$290,000).[25] Mumbai bought five players in the auction, including one capped overseas player.[26][27]

League stage

[edit | edit source]

Mumbai Indians began their season with a win against Kolkata for the first time since the 2012 season.[35] They lost their next four matches to Delhi Capitals,[36] Rajasthan Royals,[37] Royal Challengers Bengaluru[38] and Punjab Kings.[39] They won their next match against Gujarat;[40] but lost the next three matches to Chennai Super Kings,[41] Sunrisers Hyderabad[42] and Chennai again.[43] They won their next match against Lucknow,[44] but lost to Bengaluru[45] and were eliminated from the season.[46] They won their next match against Punjab,[47] but lost the last two matches of the season to Kolkata[48] and Rajasthan[49] to finish the league stage at the ninth place with eight points.[50]
